claim: _humanize_label turns a lowercase snake_case identifier into a readable label by splitting on underscores, capitalizing each word, and fully upper-casing words in _ACRONYMS (customer_id -> 'Customer ID', total_amount_usd -> 'Total Amount USD', q1_2024 -> 'Q1 2024').
_ACRONYMS = {id,url,api,db,sql,ip,uuid,usd} satisfies the AC-required minimum acronym set (id,url,api,db,sql,ip,uuid) plus usd for the total_amount_usd worked example.

_SNAKE_CASE_IDENTIFIER regex ^[a-z0-9]+(?:_[a-z0-9]+)*$ matches only lowercase snake_case identifiers; anything with uppercase, space, punctuation, non-ASCII, or leading/trailing/doubled underscore fails to match and is returned verbatim by _humanize_label.
_humanize_label is idempotent: a humanized label (containing a space or uppercase, or a pure-digit word) passes back through unchanged.

_compute_table_payload adds an additive column_labels list (humanized) parallel to columns; the raw columns list stays the identity key and column_types keys off raw str_columns, so raw names are unchanged (AC #6).

The binary-search row-trim loop now sets payload row_count=mid and truncated=total-mid before measuring each candidate, and sets final row_count=lo, truncated=total-lo after the loop, keeping row_count+truncated==total.

_default_axis_label fills a chart axis's label from the humanized field only when the axis is a dict with a non-empty string field and an empty/None/whitespace label; an LLM-set non-empty label is preserved exactly; a non-dict axis or missing field is returned unchanged (AC #3, #4).
_compute_chart_payload applies _default_axis_label to spec x and y only; series is carried through unchanged (spec.get('series')), so legend/series names are unchanged (AC #7).

_display_labels returns column_labels when it is a list of the same length as columns, otherwise falls back to raw columns; shared by the Markdown table serializer and one-row small-result path so the two surfaces cannot drift.

_table_block_to_markdown and _small_result_to_markdown render the header from _display_labels (humanized when present), giving the Markdown fallback the same header as the widget (AC #2); the separator/keying still use raw columns.
_render_dataframe emits a column_labels field (humanized from str_columns) so its block stays byte-identical to the production Markdown table path.

The widget (query_results.html) reads block.column_labels into state.labels (parallel to columns), renders each header as label when present and non-empty else the raw name, and keeps sort/type/CSV keying on raw columns (AC #1, #6).

Tests assert the mapping table (customer_id->Customer ID, api_key->API Key, url->URL, etc.), idempotency, passthrough of non-snake_case/degenerate/non-ASCII names, humanized Markdown headers, additive column_labels with unchanged raw columns/column_types, chart axis default fill vs LLM-set preservation, empty-string label handling, and series untouched.
